examples.trans: Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.trans: Did you dump the entire bottle of syrup straight into this?
Here the word for 'outright, altogether' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: Did you dump the entire bottle of syrup straight into this?
Here the word for 'syrup' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: Did you dump the entire bottle of syrup straight into this?
This expression comes from 'did you pour right in?'.

meanings.en: earlier, a short while ago (same day)

examples.trans: I called earlier.
What did you say earlier?

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.

meanings.en: a lot, much, in large quantity
meanings.note: Adverbial form of 많다 (to be many/much)

examples.trans: I did a lot of work today.
Please eat plenty and enjoy.
I want to put in right now.
How about trying to put in together tomorrow?

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 나는 단 거 싫어하니까 시럽을 아예 넣지 말라 그랬지!
examples.trans: I hate sweet drinks, so I told you not to put any syrup in at all!
This expression comes from 'sweet'.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 나는 단 거 싫어하니까 시럽을 아예 넣지 말라 그랬지!
examples.trans: I hate sweet drinks, so I told you not to put any syrup in at all!
This expression comes from 'because I dislike'.

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.en: to hold, to carry in one's hand
meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb; 들고 가다 means 'to carry along'.

examples.trans: Please take your bag with you.
If it's heavy, I'll carry it.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for eating a meal or food; honorific equivalent is 드시다.

examples.trans: Let's eat lunch together.
Did you eat breakfast?

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for something near the speaker; often contracted to 이거 in speech.

examples.trans: Did you film this too?
How much is this?

meanings.en: to be how, to be in what state
meanings.note: Its adverbial form 어떻게 ('how') is used to ask how something is done or how things turned out.

examples.trans: How do you feel today?
How did the meeting turn out?

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.trans: It is just so-so—a rather predictable feel?
This expression comes from 'obvious, predictable'.

examples.text: 벌써 두 번 사고 친 것 같아서 간당간당한 느낌이에요.
examples.trans: I feel like I already messed up twice, so I am hanging by a thread.
The topic of it is a feeling came up during this shoot.

examples.text: 몰래카메라라서 알고 찍히면 티 나고 재미없대.
examples.trans: Since it is a hidden camera, they said it looks obvious and unfunny if you know beforehand.
Today's atmosphere is truly they say it is unfunny.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: Do that and they will mark you down as being defiant.
This expression comes from 'saying you are rebelling'.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 아닌데요, 저는 진짜 빤하고 올드한 것 같아서 그렇게 말씀드린 건데요.
examples.trans: Not at all—I only said so because it genuinely felt predictable and old-fashioned.
This expression comes from 'old-fashioned'.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.
Please don't say it like that.
It's not that difficult compared to what I thought.
I want to humbly tell him right now.
How about trying to humbly tell him together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 아니, 핑크가 어려운 게 아니라 그런 거짓말이 어렵다고요.
examples.trans: No, it is not that pink is difficult—telling that kind of lie is difficult.
Here the word for 'lie' is key.

meanings.note: Common colloquial intensifier in spoken Korean

examples.trans: The weather is really cold today.
That food is really delicious.

meanings.en: to be unable to, cannot do
meanings.note: Expresses inability; follows a noun in 말 못하다 (cannot say).

examples.trans: I cannot swim.
I couldn't contact you because I was busy.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: That is why you are a cruel jerk, do you know that?
Here the word for 'guy, jerk' is key.

examples.text: 그래, 예진이 너 왜 나한테 거짓말했어?
examples.trans: Yeah, Ye-jin, why did you lie to me?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 거짓말하다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (lied).

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Colloquial intensifier (shortened from 엄청나게).

examples.trans: The weather is super cold today.
That movie was super fun.
Did you hear about this T-shirt?
I was busy today because of T-shirt.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.
This is my friend Minsu.
He/she did it all.

meanings.note: Contraction of 이 아이; used when introducing or referring to someone younger or close
Colloquial contraction of 요사이

examples.trans: How have you been doing these days?
I have too much work lately.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: Adverbial form of 이렇다.
Used to emphasize degree.

examples.trans: You can do it like this.
Why is it so cold today?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 얘 요새 왜 이렇게 반항해? 사춘기야?
examples.trans: Why is this kid rebelling like this lately—did he hit puberty?
Here the word for 'is it puberty?' is key.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
